name: GIAB genome stratifications v3.6 (GRCh38): difficult and complex regions
maintainer: NIST Genome in a Bottle Consortium with the GA4GH Benchmarking Team and the Telomere-to-Telomere Consortium
scope: BED stratifications of the GRCh38 reference into regions where variant calling or interpretation is difficult: low mappability, segmental duplications, tandem repeats and satellites, reference gaps, falsely duplicated and collapsed regions, regions of copy-number variation that cause false-positive calls, the MHC, KIR and VDJ loci, extreme-GC promoters, and the union of all difficult regions, with sex-chromosome regions. The GRCh38 set lists 189 stratification files; 23 BED files that bear on complex loci are mirrored with the set's README, background, file list and checksum list.
mapping_methods: 0-based half-open BED intervals on the GRCh38 primary-assembly chromosomes named chr1 to chrY; the names equal the UCSC-style names of the RefSeq assembly report, which is how they are joined to the 1, 2, X naming of ClinVar, gnomAD and Ensembl.

licence.name: "Publicly released data are freely available for reuse without embargo" (BACKGROUND file of the GRCh38 set, verified live); no formal licence identifier is given.
licence.redistribution: Free to reuse; the README files carry the citations that the maintainers request

update_frequency: New versions every few months to a year (the listing shows v2.0 in 2020-03 through v3.6 in 2025-04).
coverage_limitations: Stratifications describe where benchmark variant calls are difficult; they do not say whether a particular call is right or wrong
Intervals exist only on the GRCh38 primary-assembly chromosomes; a variant on an alternate or patch scaffold has no stratification here
Mappability regions are defined for short-read mapping (README)
known_omissions: The GRCh37, CHM13 and HG002 haplotype sets, the bigBED versions, and the Ancestry, GC-content, functional and genome-specific (HG001 to HG007) stratifications are not fetched
Of the 189 GRCh38 files, the remaining low-complexity (homopolymer, simple-repeat) and mappability files are not fetched
The GIAB benchmark call sets (truth variants) are not fetched

reuse_decision.rationale: Before a call in a duplicated, polymorphic or low-mappability region is interpreted, the region has to be recognised; the maintained GA4GH/GIAB stratifications are the community standard for this and are small (23 files, a few MB each), so building own masks would repeat established work.

status.notes: FTP directory with an MD5 list; all downloaded files verified against it. The set README says the files were developed with GA4GH and the T2T Consortium.

unverified_fields: how each individual stratification was derived (only the category summaries of the README were read)

mechanism_evidence.note: segmental duplications, falsely duplicated and collapsed regions, MHC, KIR and VDJ loci
tandem-repeat, satellite and homopolymer regions where small-variant calls are unreliable

evidence_profile.biological_context: Regions defined from reference-sequence features and read mappability, not from the biology of any sample: segmental duplications and paralogous regions, highly polymorphic immune loci (MHC, KIR, VDJ), falsely duplicated or collapsed reference regions, tandem repeats and reference gaps.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Region annotations from the GIAB and GA4GH benchmarking effort. Membership of a region is a property of the reference and of short-read mappability, not a measurement of any variant call.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Not applicable to mechanism. A region flag says a call there is less reliable or that a paralog may be involved; it cannot separate a true variant from a mis-mapped paralogous sequence variant.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: None: region membership carries no phenotype information.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A position outside every listed region is not guaranteed to be reliably callable: the sets stratify benchmark performance and do not certify individual calls. A call inside a region must not be discarded or trusted on that basis alone.
